page: Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is a High Performance family cloud server featuring 12 vCPUs and 24.0 GB of RAM. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz, the system utilizes 6 physical cores with hyper-threading under a shared CPU allocation model. The processor includes 16 MB of L3 cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES cryptography. Local storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations place this server consistently in the average performance tier. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1189.0 and a multi-core score of 8081.0, with software compilation via Clang reaching 15337.0. In stress-ng testing, the server records 1418.58 for single-core and 17309.27 for multi-core operations. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read bandwidth of 1224.9 GB/sec, dropping to 87.74 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.62 GB/sec for uncached writes.

The server demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, processing 18.53 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 4095.21 in Passmark database tests. Static web serving throughput is robust at 11.99 GB/sec. However, resource limitations are evident in machine learning tasks; while small 135M LLM inference runs at 142.19 tokens/sec for text generation, medium 7B LLM inference drops to a weak 7.43 tokens/sec, and large 70B models are unsupported. The shared CPU allocation presents a potential performance tradeoff under sustained, heavy compute loads. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, web serving, and database workloads that benefit from NVMe storage without requiring dedicated CPU cores.
description: The Vultr vhp-12c-24gb-intel is an x86_64 High Performance cloud server configured with 12 shared Intel Xeon vCPUs (6 physical cores with hyper-threading) operating at 2.0 GHz, 24.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD. It features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES. Benchmark results indicate solid mid-tier performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8081.0, a Passmark CPU score of 17934.88, and a high Redis throughput of 18.53 million SET operations per second. While highly capable for static web serving at 11.99 GB/sec and software compilation, its shared CPU architecture and weak medium-model LLM inference speeds (7.43 tokens/sec for 7B models) make it less suitable for heavy AI workloads. It represents a cost-effective option for database hosting, multi-threaded processing, and general web serving.
